The lower half of the frame is calm open water with soft ripples and long reflections, completely empty in the near water and across the left two-thirds: no boats, no quay, no posts, no rocks, nothing close to the camera. The shore and everything on it sit in the middle distance, small with distance. Nothing later than 1470 anywhere: no cars, street lamps, power lines, tyres, concrete, plastic, glass windows, motorboats, ferries, modern clothing, Baroque spires, modern bridges. No text, no border, no watermark.

A photorealistic photograph of a real full-size Hanseatic holk of about 1460, the big northern cargo ship of the Baltic and the North Sea: about 26 metres long, a very broad, deep, round-bellied hull with clinker-built overlapping planks, a strongly curved banana-shaped sheer rising high at both ends, a square sterncastle and a small forecastle built onto the hull, one tall mast with a single very large square sail of undyed linen with a bonnet laced to its foot, a round fighting top at the masthead, and a small lateen mizzen. A plain working ship: no carving, no gilding, no windows, no flags, no gunports. Seen exactly side-on, bow pointing right, warm late afternoon light from the right, the same light and style as the reference photo. Weathered sails, hemp rigging, dark tarred planking. Not a fantasy ship, not a pirate ship, not a model: a real ship, photographed. She is isolated on a solid, flat, evenly lit chroma-key green background (#00b140) filling everything around her, including below the hull: no sea, no sky, no shadow, no floor, no stand, no cradle. The whole ship from the mastheads to the keel in frame, with a margin all round.
